requirements.text: The Correlator Backend System must receive data from the Correlator in real-time.
The Correlator Backend System must assemble time-series from the Correlator lag output.
The Correlator Backend System must perform Fourier Transforms of the assembled time series.
The Correlator Backend System must perform a limited number of additional processes upon user request.
The Correlator Backend System must deliver suitably formatted results to the End-to-End System.
The BE shall receive LTA or Speed Dump Lag Frames from the Correlator.
The transfer shall take place in such a manner that all data needed to perform any Fourier Transform shows-up on a single processor.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, State Count data produced by the Correlator.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, data and parameters specific to the current EVLA Observational Mode needed for processing the Correlator Lag values.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, all meta-data necessary to format BE results for delivery to the E2E.
The BE shall provide operational status data to and receive control data from the M&C System.
The BE shall provide error and warning reports to M&C as operating conditions warrant.
The BE shall provide several optionally selectable levels of printed messages detailing operational parameters at critical locations in the system.
The BE shall deliver formatted final results to the e2e System.
The BE shall acknowledge receipt of all data received from M&C.
The BE shall notify M&C of any detected interruptions of data delivery from the Correlator.
The BE shall verify successful delivery of output to the e2e.
The BE shall guarantee safe delivery of all internal messages.
The BE shall be able to handle lag frames of less than 128 values.
The BE shall be able to handle lag sets up to a maximum size of 262,144 values.
All users of the system shall login using some form of unique identification.
All login attempts shall be done in a secure manner.
A system administrator shall have unrestricted access to all aspects of the system.

All login attempts shall be encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher, and authentication shall be performed against a centralized directory service (e.g., LDAP/Active Directory) using strong, salted password hashing.

The system shall maintain an immutable, time-stamped audit log of all administrative actions, login attempts, and privilege changes, which must be exported to a secure, centralized log management system.

Administrative access shall be governed by the principle of least privilege, requiring multi-factor authentication for high-impact operations and separating administrative roles to prevent single-point-of-compromise.
The system shall provide a buffer capable of storing at least 60 minutes of processed data to handle e2e system outages.
The system shall cache at least 5 minutes of incoming correlator data during M&C connectivity loss.
The system shall provide storage capacity for 100% of the maximum input data rate for a burst duration of 30 seconds, plus a 20% standby reserve.
The system shall resume full operational status from idle/standby mode within 30 seconds.
The architecture shall support a modular upgrade path to accommodate a 4x increase in aggregate data input throughput over the initial 1.6 Gbytes/sec specification.
Define the specific memory capacity in GB and the required memory bandwidth in GB/s based on the 1.6 Gbytes/sec input stream.
Define the maximum burst size in Gbytes and the duration in seconds that the system must buffer without data loss.
Specify the target maximum aggregate input throughput (e.g., 10 Gbytes/sec) that the architecture must support to ensure future-proofing.
Define the maximum outage duration (e.g., 300 seconds) the system must be able to buffer before data loss occurs.
Specify a maximum recovery time objective (RTO) in seconds for resuming operations from idle.
